Current code: end = min(len, offset+max_chars); then need(end>offset||offset===text.length) — but missing "move an interior end backward" logic. Contract: reject interior start, move interior end backward. Original content sha differs from provided source (a39bf... vs 21b58...). The provided utf8 in the first message is claimed to be subject.mjs sha 21b58... — that matches mutation_files hash. So the given utf8 is the current buggy source; need to restore contract behavior.

Fix: after computing end, if splitPair(end), end-=1. Then reject nonempty read that can't progress: need(end>offset || offset===text.length, 'inspection-range-splits-unicode')? Actually "reject a nonempty read that cannot make progress without splitting a pair" — if offset<len and end===offset (max_chars=1 splitting?) Actually with max_chars>=1, end>=offset+1. Moving end back could make end===offset if the unit at offset is a low surrogate... but start interior rejected, so text[offset] high surrogate; max_chars=1 → end=offset+1 splits pair → end=offset → no progress → reject. Keep need(end>offset||offset===text.length,...).
